tasks.title: Paid but not cancelled
tasks.question: List customer ids whose cancelled_at is NULL and paid_at is not NULL.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (customer_id INTEGER, paid_at TEXT, cancelled_at TEXT);
inserts: INSERT INTO orders VALUES (4, NULL, NULL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE cancelled_at IS NULL AND paid_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY customer_id;
tasks.why_it_breaks: A model that writes `cancelled_at = NULL` silently fails because SQL NULL comparisons require `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL`.

tasks.title: June 2025 reporting window
tasks.question: Return order ids for June 2025, inclusive of June 30 but not July 1.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, order_date TEXT);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-06-01' AND order_date < '2025-07-01' ORDER BY order_id;
tasks.why_it_breaks: A common pitfall is using `<= '2025-06-30'`, which incorrectly admits July 1st boundaries or fails on timestamp precision.

tasks.title: Customer totals by paid orders
tasks.question: Return customer ids with more than one paid order and the total paid amount for each such customer.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payments (customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM payments WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY customer_id;
tasks.why_it_breaks: Models often forget to filter on paid rows first or they include customers with exactly one order, which changes both the grouping and the total.

tasks.title: Zero-value invoices are not missing
tasks.question: List invoice ids with a non-zero amount and no payment date, but do not treat zero as missing.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE invoices (invoice_id INTEGER, amount REAL, paid_at TEXT);
inserts: INSERT INTO invoices VALUES (5, NULL, NULL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT invoice_id FROM invoices WHERE amount IS NOT NULL AND amount != 0 AND paid_at IS NULL ORDER BY invoice_id;
tasks.why_it_breaks: Zero is a valid numeric value, not NULL. Models often conflate missing values with zero when writing filters.

tasks.title: Exclude cancelled shipments
tasks.question: Find orders that shipped and were not later cancelled. A refund entry should not cause a valid order to be excluded.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, shipped_at TEXT, cancelled_at TEXT, refund_amount REAL);
inserts: INSERT INTO orders VALUES (24, '2025-03-14', NULL, NULL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL ORDER BY order_id;
tasks.why_it_breaks: Many models treat refund rows or non-cancellation flags as evidence of a cancellation problem, even when the order was never cancelled.
